concept.technique_name: context clue analysis across paired blanks

examples.problem_statement: Directions: select one entry for each blank from the corresponding column of choices; fill all blanks in the way that best completes the text. Human nature and long distances have made exceeding the speed limit a (i) ______ in the state, so the legislators surprised no one when, acceding to public demand, they (ii) ______ increased penalties for speeding. Blank (i): (A) controversial habit, (B) cherished tradition, (C) disquieting ritual. Blank (ii): (D) endorsed, (E) considered, (F) rejected.

solution.operation: Read the clue phrase "human nature and long distances" and note what it implies about speeding in this state
solution.result: Exceeding the speed limit is rather routine for drivers there
solution.description: Mine the opening clause for the clue the sentence gives you: human nature plus long distances explains why drivers habitually speed, so the state's attitude toward speeding is casual and routine rather than fraught.

solution.operation: Match "routine" against the Blank (i) choices: controversial habit / cherished tradition / disquieting ritual
solution.description: Test each Blank (i) option against the routine reading. Nothing in the sentence suggests speeding here is "controversial" or "disquieting," so those two are unsupported; "cherished tradition" is the one that fits a routine, accepted practice.

solution.operation: Ask what the legislature would have to do about increased penalties so that it "surprised no one"
solution.result: The action must be consistent with speeding being a cherished tradition and with public demand
solution.description: Set up Blank (ii) by using the sentence's own logic: the legislators' act is described as unsurprising and as acceding to public demand, so whatever fills the blank must line up with a public that cherishes speeding.

solution.operation: Match that requirement against the Blank (ii) choices: endorsed / considered / rejected
solution.description: Test each Blank (ii) option. Given what the sentence has established, it would be surprising if the legislature "endorsed" or even "considered" harsher speeding penalties; only "rejected" leaves the outcome unsurprising.

solution.operation: Combine the two selected entries into the answer pair
solution.result: cherished tradition (Choice B) and rejected (Choice F)
solution.description: Report one entry per column, as the directions require, and re-read the completed sentence to confirm the two choices support each other.

examples.answer: Choice B: cherished tradition; Choice F: rejected

key_reminders: Each blank is decided by evidence inside the sentence, not by which word sounds most sophisticated.
"Surprised no one" signals that the blank must agree with the attitude already established, not contrast with it.
In a two-blank text completion, the two entries must produce one coherent sentence together.
common_mistakes: Reading "acceding to public demand" as demand for tougher penalties, which pushes you toward "endorsed" and reverses the sentence's logic.
Choosing "controversial habit" because increased penalties feel like a dispute, even though the sentence never presents speeding as contested.
Settling for "considered" as a safe middle option, when mere consideration would still be surprising in a state where speeding is cherished.

concept.technique_name: dividing an A.P. by a common product to expose an H.P.

examples.problem_statement: Let the positive numbers a, b, c, d be in A.P. Then the type of progression for the numbers abc, abd, acd, bcd is:

solution.operation: a, b, c, d \text{ in A.P.}
solution.result: The four given numbers form an arithmetic progression
solution.description: Write down the given condition as the starting sequence; every later line is a transformation of this one sequence.

solution.result: These four quotients are also in A.P.
solution.description: Divide every term of the A.P. by the same positive quantity abcd. Scaling all terms of an arithmetic progression by one nonzero constant keeps the common difference proportional, so the result is still an A.P.

solution.result: This simplified sequence is in A.P.
solution.description: Cancel the shared factor in each quotient: a over abcd leaves 1 over bcd, b over abcd leaves 1 over acd, and so on. The A.P. property carries over from the previous line untouched.

solution.result: bcd, acd, abd, abc are in H.P., i.e. the reciprocals of the A.P. terms form the harmonic progression
solution.description: Invert each term. By definition a sequence whose reciprocals form an A.P. is a harmonic progression, so taking reciprocals of the step 3 sequence returns the products asked about and identifies their progression type.

key_reminders: Dividing (or multiplying) every term of an A.P. by the same nonzero constant leaves it an A.P.
A sequence is in H.P. exactly when the sequence of its reciprocals is in A.P.
a/(abcd) simplifies to 1/(bcd): the numerator cancels one factor of the product.
common_mistakes: Dividing by abcd but forgetting to cancel, so the 1/bcd form never appears and the H.P. link stays hidden.
Mismatching which product pairs with which letter: a over abcd gives 1/bcd, not 1/abc.
Concluding the products abc, abd, acd, bcd are themselves in A.P., since it is their reciprocals that inherit the arithmetic structure.
